title: 还没(有)…呢: not yet
summary: Lets you say something hasn't happened yet, as in 我还没吃饭呢.
structure: Subject + 还没(有) + Verb (+ Object) (+ 呢)
explanation:
还没(有) + verb means 'not yet': 我还没吃饭 'I haven't eaten yet.' 呢 at the end is very common and adds 'still waiting': 他还没来呢 'He's not here yet.' As with 没, there is no 了.

It's the natural answer to a 了吗 question when the thing hasn't happened yet: 你吃饭了吗？— 还没呢 'Not yet.'

examples.en: I haven't been to Shanghai yet.

mistakes.why: Don't use 了 with 没; end with 呢 if you like.
The order is 还 + 没.

exercises.en: My younger brother hasn't got up yet.
why: Correct: 还没 + verb = not yet.
The order is 还 then 没.
还不 means 'still won't / still doesn't'.

exercises.prompt: Someone asks 你吃饭了吗？ and you haven't yet. You say:

why: Correct: 还没 + verb, no 了.

exercises.en: I haven't finished my homework yet.
exercises.why: 还没 + verb, and 呢 at the end.

why: Don't put 了 with 没.
没 must come before the verb.
了 doesn't go with 没.
吗 would make it a question.
